entry.title: [HIGH] MCP permission approval can return without unblocking the tool call.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS session showed MCP tools from a connected server returning `MCP tool call requires approval` even after the user tapped `Allow once` in the client permission prompt. The prompt rendered normally and produced no visible error, but retrying the same `add_repo` and `get_session` calls on the same server produced the identical approval-required response across multiple attempts and after reopening the app. The result is an approval UI that appears accepted while the underlying MCP tool state remains blocked.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Editing settings.json hook commands can fail false JSON validation.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Git Bash setup found that the Claude Code Edit tool repeatedly refused an otherwise valid `.claude/settings.json` change when the edited hook `command` string contained shell regex metacharacters such as `'.ts$'`. The tool reported `Invalid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unterminated string` and rolled the edit back, while independent `jq` validation passed before and after, and writing the same value through a structured JSON mutation succeeded immediately. The failure appears to be in the Edit tool's settings validator or patch path, not in the final JSON bytes.

entry.title: [HIGH] CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR can name a different account than the session appears to spend.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code Desktop and CLI setup with several config roots found that a desktop-launched session exposed `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `claude auth status`, and model-visible context for one account while desktop session records, usage samples, and owner confirmation indicated another account was being billed. Follow-up measurements found contradictory account identifiers inside the same config file, including an OAuth identity for one account and cached usage for another. The reporter explicitly notes that the signing credential was not directly measured, so the hard limitation is that local tooling cannot reliably identify the effective account or billing boundary from the available session surfaces.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash tool timeouts can background commands instead of cancelling them.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Linux repro found that a Bash tool call with a 3s timeout returned control to the agent while the underlying process continued running for roughly 16 more seconds. The reporter tied the behavior to multi-hour VM disk-saturation incidents under concurrent subagent load, where many individually timed-out commands could continue consuming I/O after the tool layer appeared to have moved on.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Resume picker search can miss retained sessions outside the 50 most recent.
entry.summary: A reported Linux Claude Code 2.1.233 repro found that both the in-session `/resume` picker and standalone `claude --resume` picker load only the 50 most recent sessions, and the type-to-search filter searches only that loaded subset rather than all retained transcript files on disk. A month-old session whose generated title contained the search term was not findable until its transcript file mtime was moved back into the top 50. This means a high `cleanupPeriodDays` setting can retain old transcripts without making them discoverable in the UI.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Security heuristics can silently discard Bash allow rules from permissions.allow.
entry.summary: A reported macOS Claude Code 2.1.233 repro found that some `permissions.allow` Bash rules remained in `.claude/settings.local.json` but disappeared from `/permissions` after a fresh session load and were not honored at execution time. In the example, `Bash(echo:*)`, `Bash(npx tsc:*)`, and `Bash(realpath:*)` loaded, while similarly formed `Bash(python3:*)` and `Bash(npm run:*)` were absent. The per-call annotation then distinguished matched allow rules from auto-mode classifier approvals, showing the discarded rules did not participate in permission matching.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Background agent view can collide session IDs and hide existing session history.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Windows background-agents view failure showed existing sessions opening with only the most recent user message visible, new sessions failing because a generated session ID was already in use, and one completed row showing an exit-before-init session error. The reporter checked `~/.claude/projects/...` and found the transcript JSONL files still present at expected sizes and mtimes, so the issue appears to affect the agent-view/session-registry layer rather than deleting transcript data. The same report noted several job directories created within minutes, including one whose ID matched the collision but had no corresponding project transcript.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Channel events can be silently invisible to non-interactive print-mode sessions.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Windows channel test found that events sent to a custom channel in a `-p` non-interactive session were accepted by the channel server but never surfaced in the model context, while the same channel did surface events in an interactive session. The reporter measured server-side acknowledgements for both queued-before-start and queued-during-run events, but the print-mode session saw the messages only after explicitly polling with the channel's read tool. Because the channel server records successful delivery, automation can falsely believe the model received a push event.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Hooks cannot watch file changes independent of the originating tool.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code hook limitation notes that PreToolUse and PostToolUse matchers fire on the Claude Code tool name, such as Edit, Write, Bash, or PowerShell, rather than on the underlying filesystem mutation. A hook that normalizes or audits written files after Edit or Write therefore does not fire when a script, shell redirection, or another tool changes the same file. There is no documented hook scope that means `run after any file content changed` regardless of which tool caused the change.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Reconnected MCP tools can ignore bypass-permissions and allow rules.
entry.summary: A reported macOS Claude Code Desktop session showed MCP server tools prompting on every call after the desktop app restarted or the server reconnected, even though `defaultMode` was `bypassPermissions` and both wildcard and per-tool allow rules were configured. Built-in Bash, Read, Edit, and Write still respected the configuration, but reconnected MCP tools such as `claude-in-chrome` displayed recurring per-call dialogs. The reporter also observed that Allow once did not suppress the next call, and Always allow did not persist across the next reconnect.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Custom sandbox proxy settings can silently remove allowlist and credential-mask controls.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.220 WSL2 documentation gap found that setting a custom sandbox proxy port made the built-in network allowlist stop enforcing `strictAllowlist` or `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, while credential `mask` entries no longer substituted secrets even with the documented `tlsTerminate` setting. The same report also found that `sandbox.credentials` denied built-in Read access to protected files despite docs saying the setting affects sandboxed Bash only. The issue is framed as a documentation gap because these controls change behavior by configuration path without an obvious warning.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Auto mode can miss agent-authored scripts that run destructive `git clean` commands.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 native Windows session in `permissions.defaultMode: "auto"` allowed a subagent to write and execute a PowerShell script whose non-terminal `Push-Location` failure left execution in the live workspace root before running `git clean -xdff`. The configured deny rules and PreToolUse hook could not inspect the script payload behind the executed file path, Windows had no Claude Code OS sandbox, and the auto-mode classifier did not block the destructive payload. The reported result was large gitignored-workspace data loss, including projects with no remote copy.

entry.title: [HIGH] Sandbox network allowlists can be bypassed by an in-sandbox CONNECT relay.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Linux sandbox configuration with `sandbox.enabled`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, `failIfUnavailable: true`, and `allowManagedDomainsOnly: true` blocked a direct HTTPS request to a non-allowlisted host with HTTP 403, but allowed the same destination when the sandboxed command forwarded the CONNECT through a local relay process. The reporter observed both paths in the same session with the same proxy credentials and same target authority, so the configured domain allowlist was active for direct requests but ineffective for relayed CONNECT traffic.

entry.title: [LOW] Agent SDK subagent docs can omit fork-mode foreground/background precedence.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Agent SDK documentation gap found that the SDK subagents page describes foreground versus background behavior for the SDK default, but does not mention fork mode, that fork mode can be enabled in the SDK, that it became the default in interactive sessions, or that `run_in_background` can be absent from the Agent tool schema while fork mode is active. The separate sub-agents docs page contains the precedence list, but the SDK page can lead users to file or debug the wrong issue when interactive CLI behavior differs from the SDK default.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Desktop dev-server start prompts can ignore bypass-permissions mode.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Desktop macOS session with permission mode set to `Bypass permissions` still showed an `Allow Claude to start dev?` approval dialog when the browser-preview flow tried to run `npm run dev` from a `.claude/worktrees/...` directory. The dialog offered only Deny or Allow once, and the reporter could not find a settings permission rule or always-allow option that suppressed the prompt. If the prompt is an intentional always-ask desktop action, the docs did not name dev-server starts as one of those exceptions.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Hook `if` conditions require tool-specific copies for one policy.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 hooks limitation found that `hooks[].if` uses permission-rule syntax, so the condition must name a single tool such as `Edit(**/*.ts)` or `Write(**/*.ts)`. A prompt hook that wants to apply the same policy to Edit, Write, and MultiEdit has to clone the handler and duplicate the prompt once per tool even though `matcher` already selected the tools. The apparently generic form `*(**/*.ts)` did not fire for a matching Write call and produced no warning, leaving the hook silently inert.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Queued input modes can run out of the order typed.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 interactive-mode documentation gap found that queued plain prompts, queued `!` shell commands, and queued slash commands do not all drain through the same path. Plain prompts can be folded into the running turn at a tool-call boundary, while `!` shell commands and most slash commands wait until the turn finishes. A user can therefore type a shell command, then a normal prompt, and have the later prompt affect the running turn before the earlier shell command executes, with no transcript or queue UI warning that the ordering changed.

entry.title: [HIGH] Sandbox `apply-seccomp` EINVAL failures can trigger unsafe retries.
entry.summary: Reported Claude Code 2.1.232 and 2.1.233 Linux sessions with `sandbox.enabled` saw intermittent Bash failures where `apply-seccomp: unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER): Invalid argument` replaced the command output. The root report traced the failure to a race where the embedded seccomp helper calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` while the runtime still has a recently exited thread in the thread group, producing EINVAL. The user-facing risk is larger than a flaky command: one agent misdiagnosed the sandbox behavior from the helper error, and another retried with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` after transient failures, successfully reading data the sandbox had blocked.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] User-level `paths:` rules can silently load nowhere.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS setup placed `paths:` frontmatter on a rule under `~/.claude/rules/`. The rule was skipped at `session_start` because it was conditional, but it also never loaded on matching file reads because user-scope rules did not appear to participate in `path_glob_match`. Project-scoped path rules matched the same file normally, and the missing user rule did not appear in `/context`, leaving a syntactically valid global convention with zero effect and no warning.

entry.title: [HIGH] Subagent compound Bash can bypass sandbox read-deny protection.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS background/job session declared sandbox filesystem `read.denyOnly` coverage for `.env*` paths and had top-level protected-path reads blocked elsewhere in the same session. A general-purpose Agent subagent then ran a compound multi-line Bash command containing `grep` against `.env.local`; the command returned real environment variable names with exit code 0, no prompt, no permission error, and no block log. The same path with `cat` would have exposed secret values to the subagent context.
